cpu_tuning_observation.hardware_pstate: no_hwp file absent, which means HWP is enabled
cpu_tuning_observation.verdict: CPU tuning is already performance-maximal. Governor performance plus EPP performance plus turbo enabled plus HWP enabled is the full performance envelope exposed by intel_pstate on this CPU. No further host-side tuning gain is available. The i5-6500T is a 4-core, 4-thread part with no hyperthreading, so per-core throughput cannot be improved by tuning.
remaining_untuned: C-state residency: deep states C6, C7s and C8 are available and are likely entered at load 0.61. Latency-sensitive guests could be served better by restricting the deepest states, at the cost of power. Not measured: cpuidle residency counters were not read.

findings.statement: CT 102 named cynic-agent-host is stopped with uptime 0, mem 0 and disk 0 for the current run only. It ran for roughly five weeks as the Hermes agent-host between its creation on 2026-09-01T17:32:27Z and the host reboot on 2026-10-06T13:10:38Z. It was NOT relaunched at the following boot because its config carries no onboot key, while all four sibling guests declare onboot=1. Its config is unprivileged=1, ostype=ubuntu, cores=2, memory=4096, swap=1024, net0 ip 10.10.10.102/24 hwaddr BC:24:11:C3:EE:79, rootfs local-lvm:vm-102-disk-1 32G. It is the target of repo slice C0.1 whose checkpoint verdict was ready, and it is absent from infra/registry.json. Before the LXC incarnation it was the QEMU VM cynic-vm-anvil on scsi0 local-lvm:vm-102-disk-0 32256M, backed up 2026-06-16 and destroyed 2026-08-29.
proof_refs: pvesh get /nodes/pve/lxc/102/config --output-format json returns NO onboot key, while 100, 101, 103 and 105 each return onboot 1
grep ':102:' /var/log/pve/tasks/index shows vzcreate OK then vzstart OK on 2026-09-01 (UPID 6A96F00B and 6A96F027), then vzshutdown OK on 2026-10-06 (UPID 6AC4D72E) with no subsequent vzstart
/var/log/pve/tasks/active shows stopall UPID 6AC4D72D followed by vzshutdown:100, :101, :103, :105 and :102 all OK, then startall UPID 6AC4D863 that relaunches only 100, 101, 103 and 105
pvesh get /cluster/resources shows lxc/102 status stopped, name cynic-agent-host, uptime 0, mem 0, disk 0
pvesh get /nodes/pve/lxc/102/config returns arch amd64, cores 2, hostname cynic-agent-host, memory 4096, nameserver 10.10.10.1, ostype ubuntu, swap 1024, unprivileged 1
head -5 /var/lib/vz/dump/vzdump-qemu-102-2026_06_16-16_55_57.log shows Starting Backup of VM 102 (qemu) and VM Name: cynic-vm-anvil

Its IP 10.10.10.102 is configured but currently unreachable (ping 100 percent packet loss). The failure mode is declaration drift with a silent availability consequence: a declared-ready service has been down for more than 24 hours with nothing in the registry to surface it.

nvme_capacity_proof.operator_claim: operator asserted the NVMe lies about its capacity and is a scam
nvme_capacity_proof.my_first_answer_was_wrong: I argued nsze == ncap == 4000787030016 therefore the capacity is authentic. That was a sophism: it measured the internal consistency of the claim, not the truth of the backing flash. A firmware that intends to deceive reports a plausible size, and nsze == ncap is exactly what such firmware must report to look honest.

identity_evidence.interpretation: nqn.2018-05.com.example is the documentation placeholder namespace reserved by NVMe-Express; no manufacturer emits it. A real device reports nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress:uuid:<uuid>. The O000397 token in the NQN is the letter O followed by the serial, so the NQN was constructed FROM the serial rather than by a manufacturer. sn 000397 is the six digits of the model label, which a real serial never is.

definitive_test.method: loop device over the raw NVMe with an offset, so the partition table was never touched
definitive_test.read_back: mkfs.ext4: Input/output error while writing out and closing file system
definitive_test.kernel_log: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 9491968 op 0x1:(WRITE) flags 0x4800 ; nvme nvme0: Disabling device after reset failure: 0 ; loop: Write error at byte offset 5368643584, length 4096
definitive_test.collateral_damage: none: all five guests (100, 101, 102, 103, 105) remained running, verified by lxc-start process count
definitive_test.cleanup: umount, rmdir, losetup -d, temp file removed; loop device count back to 0
definitive_test.verdict: PROVEN. The controller reports a 4 TB namespace, accepts Identify commands, and fails every WRITE with EIO until it disables itself. The capacity is fabricated. The operator was right and my nsze==ncap argument was wrong.

nvme_capacity_proof.note_on_media_errors: The 3680 media_errors reported by smart-log are consistent with a device that has no real flash behind the namespace, not with a worn SSD. They were never wear counters on a working drive.

retracted_measurement.claim: iowait is 86.11 percent of CPU time
retracted_measurement.origin: iowait ticks divided by total ticks from /proc/stat
retracted_measurement.why_retracted: that arithmetic is invalid here: cumulative idle ticks were 3213552 while iowait ticks were 32242650, so idle was smaller than iowait, which cannot hold on a host whose storage is not limiting. On an LXC host the time guests spend waiting on storage is accounted differently. The instantaneous vmstat reading of 1 to 2 percent is the trustworthy figure.
retracted_measurement.lesson: cumulative tick ratios must be sanity checked against the idle tick count before being reported as a saturation percentage

build_performance_diagnosis.question: where is the real build throughput bottleneck on proxmox-forge
build_performance_diagnosis.verdict: a deliberate single-job cargo setting, not the disk and not the CPU, is the dominant bottleneck; it costs 56 percent of full-workspace build time

peak_rss_per_crate_kbytes.note: Maximum resident set size is the largest single rustc peak observed, not a sum over concurrent jobs. The two heaviest crates are cynic-mcp and cynic-protocol at about 1.1 GiB each.

why_jobs_one_was_set.stated_justification_in_repo: rustc can overflow or ICE on deep monomorphization, serde plus rmcp being 47 percent of IR, citing rust-lang/rust 103767, 122357 and 138561; -j 1 stated as the only reliable setting and -j 2 as flaky under memory pressure
why_jobs_one_was_set.assessment: the ICE risk is a real rustc property that cannot be dismissed, but the memory justification was never quantified in the repository. It is now quantified: one rustc peaks at about 1.1 GiB, so two jobs cost about 2.2 GiB against 7.7 GiB available with zero swaps. The stated memory pressure does not exist on this builder.
why_jobs_one_was_set.drift_from_observed_toolchain: three toolchain versions coexist in the repository. rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.95.0 and overrides the builder, whose /bin/rustc reports 1.93.0 outside a checkout; the effective rustc inside a build is 1.95.0, confirmed by rustup show active-toolchain reporting "1.95.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (overridden by <checkout>/rust-toolchain.toml)". The pre-existing comments in .cargo/config.toml cite 1.96, a version no checkout actually runs. The measurements in this checkpoint were taken at 1.95.0.
why_jobs_one_was_set.toolchain_drift_is_itself_unresolved: whether the jobs=1 setting was calibrated against 1.93.0, 1.95.0 or 1.96 is not recorded anywhere in the repository. The prior comment named 1.96 for the clippy ICE and 1.96 for the incremental ghost errors, neither of which matches the toolchain that builds actually use.

ruled_out_as_bottleneck.cpu_capacity: load 1.70 across 4 cores, idle 47 to 73 percent during the build; the cores were idle because parallelism was pinned to one, not because the machine lacked capacity
ruled_out_as_bottleneck.network: wifi 5 GHz at -57 dBm, 526 Mbit/s negotiated, 0.027 ms round trip to mesh peers
ruled_out_as_bottleneck.sequential_bandwidth: 103 MB/s host read and 86.5 to 114 MB/s writes inside the builder, correct for a rotational disk
ruled_out_as_bottleneck.page_cache_management: Cached 1.2 GiB, Dirty 0.34 percent of MemTotal, Writeback 0, vm.dirty_ratio 20 and dirty_background_ratio 10 both at kernel defaults. No backlog and no misconfiguration. An earlier claim in this session that the cache held 8.2 GiB was stale and is retracted.

nvme_purchase_case_after_this_diagnosis.recommendation: the configuration change dominates the hardware purchase for build throughput. Storage remains justified on other grounds: it removes a device that returned EIO on every write, and it cuts the 2m28s boot observed with systemd-analyze. Those are risk and predictability arguments, not build speed.

not_proven: that two jobs never triggers the rustc ICE on a future commit: four clean runs bound the risk, they do not eliminate it, and the monomorphisation that triggers the ICE varies per crate
that two jobs is the optimal setting: jobs 3 and 4 were never measured, and the memory projection for them rests on the single observed 1.1 GiB peak rather than on measurement
that jobs 1 and 2 differ by 56 percent on every future commit: the single-job figure is one measurement on one commit, while the two-job figures are four

repetition_across_commits.purpose: verify that the two-job gain is stable and does not trigger the rustc ICE cited in .cargo/config.toml
repetition_across_commits.method: full workspace cargo build --offline with a fresh target directory per commit, two jobs forced on the command line, wall clock and peak RSS captured with /usr/bin/time

two_job_statistics.toolchain_used: 1.95.0, overridden by rust-toolchain.toml inside each checkout

memory_evidence.interpretation: two concurrent jobs did not double the peak. The additional 89 MiB is direct evidence that the two crates compiling at the same moment are of unequal size, which is also why the wall clock roughly halves instead of quartering.

repetition_across_commits.conclusion: the two-job gain reproduces across four distinct commits with a 34 second spread and zero compiler errors and zero internal compiler errors, under rustc 1.95.0 as pinned by rust-toolchain.toml. The measurement is stable enough to propose a configuration change, while remaining an observation and not a guarantee for every future commit.
